name: Holden Dealer Team (HDT)
overview: Holden Dealer Team (HDT) Special Vehicles was established in 1980 by nine-time Bathurst champion Peter Brock at 124 Bertie Street, Port Melbourne. When Holden withdrew factory motorsport funding in 1979, Brock purchased the team with financial backing from a coalition of Holden dealers. HDT transformed showroom Commodores into bespoke high-performance road cars with hand-assembled blueprint V8 engines, Bilstein suspension, Scheel sports seats, Momo steering wheels, and wind-tunnel aero bodykits. HDT created Australia's most revered homologation muscle car—the 1985 VK SS Group A 'Blue Meanie'—alongside the VC Brock Commodore, VH Group 3, and VL Group A before Brock's split with Holden in 1987. Today, HDT builds retro heritage editions.
australian_history:
The Holden Dealer Team originated in 1969 when Harry Firth created a semi-works team for Holden. Peter Brock joined in 1969, scoring his first Bathurst win in an LJ Torana GTR XU-1 in 1972. When GM-Holden ended direct factory backing in 1979, Brock negotiated with the Holden Dealer Network to acquire the team, launching HDT Special Vehicles in 1980.

HDT's first road car, the 1980 VC HDT Commodore, was an instant triumph: 500 numbered cars in Firethorn Red, Palais White, and Tuxedo Black with 5.0L (160kW) and 4.2L V8s, Irmscher wheels, and Bilstein dampers. This was followed by the VH Group 1, Group 2, and Group 3 (with Brock's signature high-output 180kW 5.0L V8). In 1983, HDT expanded into luxury with the WB Magnum Statesman.

In 1985, to homologate the Commodore for international Group A touring car rules, HDT produced 500 examples of the VK SS Group A. Painted exclusively in Formula Blue, the 'Blue Meanie' featured a de-stroked 4.9-litre (4987cc) V8 with Crane cam, roller rockers, double-row timing chain, and distinctive white Aero wheels. In 1986, HDT followed with the VL SS Group A, creating the famous 'Plus Pack'.

However, in 1986-1987, Brock championed the 'Energy Polarizer'—a small resin-filled box containing crystals and magnets that Brock claimed realigned molecular structures to improve ride and performance—and demanded Holden endorse it on the new HDT Director luxury car. When Holden technical director Ray Borrett tested the car and discovered unauthorized rear suspension modifications and no scientific validity to the Polarizer, Holden formally severed all ties with HDT in February 1987. The Brock HDT era ended, but the marque was later resurrected by Peter Champion and operates today building heritage Brock tributes.

models.name: HDT VK SS Group A ('Blue Meanie')
models.overview: The HDT VK SS Group A, universally affectionately known as the 'Blue Meanie', is the most revered homologation muscle car in Australian touring car racing history. Built by Peter Brock's Holden Dealer Team Special Vehicles at 124 Bertie Street, Port Melbourne in 1985, the Group A was created to homologate the Commodore under international FIA Group A racing regulations. All 500 cars were painted in striking Formula Blue, featuring a de-stroked 4.9-litre (4987cc) V8 with Crane cam and roller rockers, M21 4-speed manual gearbox, Scheel velour bucket seats, and distinctive white 16-inch Aero alloy wheels.

vk-group-a.name: HDT VK SS Group A ('Blue Meanie')
vk-group-a.overview: The HDT VK SS Group A, universally affectionately known as the 'Blue Meanie', is the most revered homologation muscle car in Australian touring car racing history. Built by Peter Brock's Holden Dealer Team Special Vehicles at 124 Bertie Street, Port Melbourne in 1985, the Group A was created to homologate the Commodore under international FIA Group A racing regulations. All 500 cars were painted in striking Formula Blue, featuring a de-stroked 4.9-litre (4987cc) V8 with Crane cam and roller rockers, M21 4-speed manual gearbox, Scheel velour bucket seats, and distinctive white 16-inch Aero alloy wheels.
vk-group-a.australian_market_notes: Under FIA Group A regulations, engine capacity determined vehicle minimum racing weight. The traditional Holden 308ci (5044cc) placed the Commodore into the heavy over-5,000cc weight division. HDT and Holden engineer Larry Perkins de-stroked the engine crankshaft by 0.040 inches, reducing capacity to 4,987cc (304ci) to slip beneath the 5,000cc limit and shed over 100 kg of required racing ballast. The 500 road cars were snapped up instantly by collectors and racers.

generations.summary: 500 homologation specials finished in Formula Blue; 4,987cc V8 (196kW/418Nm), Crane cam, roller rockers, Scheel interior, white 16-inch Aero wheels.
